## About

My name is Yasmin Mansour, and I am currently in the 12th semester of my medical studies at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, completing my Practical Year (final year of medical school). I am also pursuing a Doctor of Medicine (Dr. med.) degree. In addition, I am a qualified nurse and work alongside my medical studies at the University Medical Center Mainz.

## Project: Alternative polyadenylation as a marker of biological immune age

As the human body ages, the immune system undergoes functional changes that can vary between individuals and across different immune cell types. This project aims to investigate whether alternative polyadenylation (APA), a mechanism involved in the regulation of messenger RNA processing, reflects age-related changes in immune cells and can be used to determine biological immune age.

To this end, single-cell transcriptomic data from different immune cell types will be analyzed, and machine learning approaches will be used to develop an APA-based "Immune Aging Clock". Subsequently, the project will investigate how infections and vaccinations influence these age-associated APA patterns and whether such changes can be used to detect alterations in biological immune age.
